seoTitle: How to Upload Your Website to Hostinger and Go Live
metaDescription: Upload HTML files to Hostinger using File Manager: create a folder, zip your site, extract it, and move the files into place to go live.
intro: Getting a finished HTML website onto Hostinger doesn't require any coding - just Hostinger's built-in File Manager and a zipped copy of your site files. This guide walks through the hPanel dashboard, creating the right folder for your domain or subfolder, and uploading, extracting, and moving your files so the site goes live. The same process works whether you're publishing to your main domain or a new folder alongside an existing WordPress install.

steps.heading: Log into Hostinger and open hPanel
steps.body: Sign into your Hostinger account and you'll land in hPanel, the dashboard where domains, websites, email, and hosting all live under one sidebar. The Domains section shows your domain portfolio at a glance, and from Websites you can jump into the specific hosting plan you want to manage. This is your starting point regardless of whether you're uploading to a brand-new domain or an existing one.

image.caption: The Hostinger hPanel dashboard, showing the Domains section with Domain portfolio, Get a New Domain, and Transfers in the sidebar.

steps.heading: Open File Manager and find public_html
steps.body: From your hosting plan, open File Manager, then navigate into the public_html folder. If you want your website to load at your main domain — yourdomain.com — this is where the files need to sit. If another site, like WordPress, is already installed on your main domain, you'll want to upload into a new folder instead so the two don't collide.

steps.heading: Create a new folder for your site
steps.body: Click New folder in the left sidebar, type a name for it in the dialog that appears, and click Create. Hostinger will suggest existing similarly-named folders as you type, which is a useful check that you're not about to create a duplicate. This folder becomes the subfolder path your site loads under, so pick a name you're fine seeing in the URL.

image.caption: The New directory dialog in File Manager, naming a folder before clicking Create — this becomes the subfolder your site will load from.

steps.heading: Zip your site and upload it
steps.body: Before uploading, compress your entire local website into a single ZIP file — this is the most reliable way to move a full folder of HTML, CSS, JS, and image assets without missing anything along the way. Open your new folder, click Upload from the top menu, and choose File to select your ZIP. The upload starts immediately once you confirm.

image.caption: The Upload dialog inside a project folder, offering File or Folder as upload options.

steps.heading: Extract the ZIP file
steps.body: Once the upload finishes, right-click the ZIP file (or use the row's overflow menu) to bring up file actions — Info, Rename, Copy file, Move file, Permissions, Archive, Extract, Download, and Delete. Select Extract, confirm a folder name if prompted, and File Manager unpacks the archive right where the ZIP sits.

image.caption: The file actions menu for an uploaded ZIP, with Extract highlighted among options like Rename, Move file, and Download.

steps.heading: Move the extracted files into place
steps.body: Double-click into the extracted folder — if there's another folder nested inside it, open that too, since ZIP tools sometimes wrap everything in an extra layer. Select all the files, starting from the first and shift-clicking the last, then click Move from the top menu and navigate to the folder you created earlier. Confirm the move, and your files land exactly where the domain or subfolder expects them.

steps.heading: Verify the live site
steps.body: Visit your domain or subfolder URL in a browser to confirm the site loads correctly. If it doesn't show up right away, double-check that the files ended up directly inside the target folder rather than nested one level too deep — that's the most common reason a freshly uploaded HTML site shows a blank page or a 403 error instead of the homepage.

faq.question: Do I need to zip my website before uploading it to Hostinger?
faq.answer: Yes, zipping your files into a single archive before uploading is the most reliable way to make sure nothing gets left out during the transfer.

faq.question: Can I upload a website to a subfolder instead of my main domain?
faq.answer: Yes, you can create a new folder inside public_html and upload your files there if your main domain already has another site, like WordPress, installed.

faq.question: Do I need coding knowledge to upload an HTML site to Hostinger?
faq.answer: No, the process uses Hostinger's File Manager interface - creating a folder, uploading a ZIP, extracting it, and moving files - so it doesn't require any coding.

faq.question: Why isn't my site showing up after uploading to Hostinger?
faq.answer: Double check that the extracted files were moved directly into the correct folder rather than left nested inside an extra subfolder, since that's the most common reason a site doesn't display at the expected URL.
